# OpenAI Agents SDK for Rust

> A Rust port of the OpenAI Agents Python SDK: agents, a runner with tools, handoffs, guardrails,
> sessions, tracing and human-in-the-loop, provider-neutral. Behaviours are pinned to the Python
> implementation v0.23.1 and checked against it by an oracle.

## Install

```toml
opai-agents = "0.2"                                                  # core + OpenAI
opai-agents = { version = "0.2", features = ["providers", "tools"] } # presets, offline model, tools
```

```rust
use opai_agents::prelude::*;

let agent = Agent::new("Assistant").instructions("Be brief.");
let result = Runner::run(&agent, "Hello", RunOptions::new()).await?;
println!("{}", result.final_output_as_str().unwrap_or_default());
```

`opai_agents::run("instructions", "input")` picks the provider from the environment; with
`AGENTS_OFFLINE=1` it answers locally and needs no key.

## The shape of the API

- `Agent`: `instructions`, `tools`, `handoffs`, `model` / `model_name`, `model_settings`,
  `output_type`, `input_guardrails` / `output_guardrails`, `hooks`, `capability`.
- `Runner::run(agent, input, RunOptions)`, `run_streamed`, `run_blocking`, `run_state`.
- `RunOptions`: builder. `.temperature(..)`, `.max_turns(..)`, `.reasoning(..)`, `.session(..)`,
  `.provider(..)`, `.resolve_with(closure)`, `.with(value)` for typed context.
- Tools: `#[function_tool]` over `async fn`, or `FunctionTool::typed` over a `schemars` struct, or
  the `Tool` trait for something custom.
- Pausing: `FunctionTool::with_needs_resolution(true)` + `RunResult::to_state()` + `RunState::approve`
  / `reject` / `provide_output` + `Runner::run_state`.
- Guardrails: `input_guardrail` / `output_guardrail` closures returning
  `GuardrailFunctionOutput`, whose verdict is `Pass`, `Fail { reason, severity }` or `Transform`.
- Bundles: `CapabilityParts::new().tool(..).instructions(..).named("x")`, then `.capability(..)`.
  `.deferred("description")` keeps it out of the prompt until the model calls `load_capability`.
- Contracts to implement: `Tool`, `Model`, `ModelProvider`, `Session`, `TracingProcessor`,
  `Capability`, `RunStateStore`.

## Crates

`opai-agents` re-exports everything. Under it: `core` (no HTTP), `macros`, `testing`, `openai`,
`providers`, `mcp`, `sqlite`, `sessions`, `observability`, `tools`, `guardrails`.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md): quick start, crates and features, examples
- [docs/COMPAT.md](docs/COMPAT.md): support matrix: what the Python SDK has and what happens here
- [docs/DEVIATIONS.md](docs/DEVIATIONS.md): every intentional difference, with an id (D-… / X-…)
- [docs/MIGRATION-FROM-PYTHON.md](docs/MIGRATION-FROM-PYTHON.md): Python API name → Rust API name
- [docs/COMPARISON.md](docs/COMPARISON.md): how this compares with the Python SDK, Rig and ADK-Rust
- [STABILITY.md](STABILITY.md): what is stable, and the deprecation policy

## Optional

- `cargo opai new <name> --template <chat|tools|hitl>` scaffolds a project.
- `conformance/scenarios/` holds the declarative parity scenarios.

# Source: README.md

# OpenAI Agents SDK (Rust)

Rust port of the [OpenAI Agents Python SDK](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python) **v0.23.1**.

Supported now: **Agent**, **Runner** (`run` / `run_blocking` / `run_streamed`), **FunctionTool** (+ `#[function_tool]` with full `schemars` schemas), **handoffs** (`HandoffCallItem` / `HandoffOutputItem` + `handoff_span`), **structured output** (`output_type`), **run context**, **input/output guardrails**, **lifecycle hooks**, **ModelProvider** name resolution, **extended `ModelSettings`**, **local Tracing**, **Responses + Chat Completions**.

## Positioning

This is a **provider-neutral** agent SDK, not a client for the official OpenAI service. It runs
the Python SDK's agent loop (tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, HITL) on top of **any
endpoint that speaks the OpenAI Responses or Chat Completions protocol**: OpenAI itself, but also
gateways, self-hosted servers and third-party models. Point it at a different provider with a base
URL and key.

Consequently, features that exist only because OpenAI hosts them are **out of scope**: hosted tools
(web / file search, code interpreter, image generation, hosted MCP, computer, shell, apply_patch),
server-side prompts (`Agent.prompt`), the Conversations API and `responses.compact`, and OpenAI
trace export. Anything that only needs a compatible *protocol* is in scope. See
[`docs/DEVIATIONS.md`](./docs/DEVIATIONS.md#scope) for the full list.

## Crates and features

Depend on `opai-agents`; it re-exports everything below under the paths the SDK has always had.

| Crate | What it holds | Pulled in by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opai-agents-core` | agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, the run loop, sessions, tracing, and the `Model` / `ModelProvider` / `McpServer` contracts. No HTTP client, database or process spawning | always |
| `opai-agents-macros` | `#[function_tool]` | always |
| `opai-agents-testing` | `ScriptedModel` and item builders (`opai_agents::testing`) | always |
| `opai-agents-openai` | Chat Completions and Responses adapters, `OpenAIProvider`, `CompatibleProvider` | feature `openai` (**default**) |
| `opai-agents-mcp` | MCP client: stdio and streamable HTTP, tool filters, `McpServerManager` | feature `mcp` |
| `opai-agents-providers` | provider presets (DeepSeek, Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Anthropic, Ollama), the capability matrix and the offline model | feature `providers` |
| `opai-agents-sessions` | `FileSession` / `FileRunStateStore`; `SqliteSession` (file-compatible with the Python SDK); Redis and Postgres variants | features `sessions`, `sqlite`, `redis`, `postgres` |
| `opai-agents-observability` | console, JSONL and OpenTelemetry export, metrics | features `observability`, `otel` |
| `opai-agents-tools` | calculator, clock, read-only files, `web_fetch` with private networks refused | features `tools`, `webfetch` |
| `opai-agents-guardrails` | length, personal data, prompt injection, keywords, JSON Schema | feature `guardrails` |
| `opai-agents-teams` | agent teams: a lead and long-lived teammates with mailboxes, a shared task list and a budget (experimental) | feature `teams` |

```toml
opai-agents = "0.2"                                                        # core + OpenAI
opai-agents = { version = "0.2", features = ["providers", "tools", "guardrails"] }
opai-agents = { version = "0.2", features = ["mcp", "sqlite"] }            # plus MCP and SQLite
opai-agents = { version = "0.2", default-features = false }                # core only, bring your own Model
```

Features add up; `providers` is what makes `opai_agents::run` and `zero_config_options` work with
anything but OpenAI.

Contributors: each crate carries an `AGENTS.md` with its boundary rules and the traps worth
knowing before you change it (`crates/core/AGENTS.md`, `crates/mcp/AGENTS.md`, and so on).

With `default-features = false` the build contains no HTTP client. A model *name* then needs a
provider you set yourself (`RunConfig.model.provider`, or `set_default_model_provider_factory`).
With `openai`, `Runner` installs the OpenAI provider on its first call, so `OPENAI_API_KEY`
(or `OPENAI_BASE_URL`) is enough. See D-047 in [`docs/DEVIATIONS.md`](./docs/DEVIATIONS.md).

## Quick start

```rust
use opai_agents::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), AgentsError> {
    let agent = Agent::new("Assistant")
        .instructions("You only respond in haikus.")
        .model_name(std::env::var("OPENAI_MODEL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "gpt-4.1-mini".into()));
    let result = Runner::run(&agent, "Tell me about recursion.", RunOptions::new()).await?;
    println!("{}", result.final_output);
    Ok(())
}
```

`opai_agents::prelude` holds the types most programs need; everything else is at the crate root.

### Start a project

```bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/charleslyh/openai-agents-rs opai-agents-scaffold   # installs `cargo-opai`
cargo opai new my-agent              # templates: chat (default), tools, hitl
cd my-agent && AGENTS_OFFLINE=1 cargo run   # no key needed; set one to talk to a model
```

The generated project depends on `opai-agents` with `providers`, so a key in the environment (or
`AGENTS_OFFLINE=1`) is the whole setup. `--path` points it at a local checkout instead of the
published version.

## Examples

Numbered by topic. Most examples call a live OpenAI-compatible API. These run offline on a scripted model and need no key: `run_state_store`, `model_middleware`, `builtin_tools`, `providers`, `model_retry`, `handoff_advanced`, `tool_use_behavior`, `dynamic_instructions`, `extensions`, `strict_schema`; `sqlite_session` falls back to the offline model.

Required env: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL`.  
Optional: `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API` (`chat_completions` | `responses`).

Which API a model uses (D-I): `OpenAIProvider::api(..)` / `CompatibleProvider::api(..)` first, then
`set_default_openai_api()`, then **Chat Completions** (what nearly every compatible server
implements) for every server, OpenAI included. Choose Responses explicitly with `.api(Responses)`,
`set_default_openai_api(Responses)` or the `openai_responses/<model>` name prefix.
Both APIs stream standard Responses wire events such as `response.output_text.delta` (D-011). The
example harness reads `OPENAI_API` (`chat_completions` | `responses`) to override the choice.

To talk to a server that needs no key, or to route several servers by model prefix, use
`CompatibleProvider::new(base_url)` (key optional, Chat Completions by default) with
`MultiProvider`: `"local/qwen2.5"`, `"gateway/my-model"`.

The examples live in [`examples/`](./examples) — a workspace member of their own, so they depend
on `opai-agents` the way your project would rather than reaching into the SDK's internals.

Ordered like the web demo's capability checklist, one knowledge point per example. The number is the file's prefix in `examples/src/` (`01_hello.rs`); the command takes the bare name.

| # | Example | Checklist group | What it shows |
|---|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| 01 | `hello` | — | Minimal `Agent` + `Runner::run` |
| 02 | `zero_config` | — | `opai_agents::run`: provider and model from the environment, offline without a key (Rust-only) |
| 03 | `streamed` | Conversation and memory | `Runner::run_streamed` events (streaming output) |
| 04 | `memory` | Conversation and memory | `Session` multi-turn memory |
| 05 | `compaction` | Conversation and memory | `CompactingSession` context compaction |
| 06 | `file_session` | Conversation and memory | `FileSession`: a conversation in a JSONL file (Rust-only) |
| 07 | `sqlite_session` | Conversation and memory | `SqliteSession`: several conversations in one database file (Rust-only) |
| 08 | `tools` | Tools | `#[function_tool]` tool loop |
| 09 | `parallel_tools` | Tools | Parallel tool calls |
| 10 | `tool_timeout` | Tools | Tool timeout (`ErrorAsResult` / `RaiseException`) |
| 11 | `tool_recovery` | Tools | Model retries after a tool failure |
| 12 | `structured_tool` | Tools | `#[derive(ToolMeta)]` + `TypedTool`: a stateful tool type plus a separate `Args` struct; parameter descriptions, enum and range constraints, per-call approval, timeout and dependency as annotations; middleware (Rust-only) |
| 13 | `capability` | Tools | A named bundle of tools, instructions and guardrails (Rust-only) |
| 14 | `deferred_capability` | Tools | `CapabilityParts::deferred`: tools stay out of the prompt until the model loads them (Rust-only) |
| 15 | `mcp` | Tools | Local stdio MCP server with a `ToolFilter` |
| 16 | `builtin_tools` | Tools | `opai_agents::tools`: calculator, clock, `file_read`, `web_fetch` and their built-in limits (Rust-only) |
| 17 | `tool_use_behavior` | Tools | `ToolUseBehavior` and `ToolChoice`: end the run on a tool, force a tool |
| 18 | `extensions` | Tools | `RunOptions::with` and `FunctionTool::require`: typed dependencies checked before the first turn (Rust-only) |
| 19 | `handoff` | Multi-agent | Multi-agent handoff |
| 20 | `handoff_advanced` | Multi-agent | Handoff arguments, input filter, custom tool name and per-run availability |
| 21 | `agents_as_tools` | Multi-agent | `Agent.as_tool` orchestration |
| 22 | `agents_as_tools_stream` | Multi-agent | `AsToolConfig::on_stream`: watch a sub-agent's output while it runs |
| 23 | `teams` | Multi-agent | A lead and two parallel teammates with a shared task list (Rust-only) |
| 24 | `hitl` | Safety and governance | `RunOptions::resolve_with` approvals, or the explicit `RunState` JSON resume |
| 25 | `run_state_store` | Safety and governance | `FileRunStateStore`: park a paused run, resume it in another process; signing and expiry (Rust-only) |
| 26 | `always_approve` | Safety and governance | Sticky `always_approve` |
| 27 | `input_guardrail` | Safety and governance | Input guardrail tripwire |
| 28 | `output_guardrail` | Safety and governance | Output guardrail tripwire |
| 29 | `tool_input_guardrail` | Safety and governance | Tool input guardrail (reject a call) |
| 30 | `tool_output_guardrail` | Safety and governance | Tool output guardrail (redact a result) |
| 31 | `verdict_transform` | Safety and governance | `Verdict::Transform`: redact the user's input and keep going (Rust-only) |
| 32 | `builtin_guardrails` | Safety and governance | Ready-made guardrails from `opai-agents-guardrails` (Rust-only) |
| 33 | `structured_output` | Output and observability | `output_type` + typed `final_output_as::<T>()` |
| 34 | `strict_schema` | Output and observability | Strict JSON schemas: the rewrite, what it refuses and the ways out |
| 35 | `run_context` | Output and observability | `RunOptions::context` read inside a tool |
| 36 | `dynamic_instructions` | Output and observability | Instructions generated from the run context |
| 37 | `hooks` | Output and observability | `RunHooks` / `AgentHooks` |
| 38 | `model_middleware` | Output and observability | `ModelMiddleware`: redact and rewrite what is sent to the model (Rust-only) |
| 39 | `usage` | Output and observability | `RunResult::usage` |
| 40 | `tracing` | Output and observability | Custom `TracingProcessor` |
| 41 | `trace_export` | Output and observability | Batched console/JSONL export and metrics (Rust-only) |
| 42 | `console` | Output and observability | Live console: spans and the conversation, in a browser (Rust-only) |
| 43 | `cancel` | Run control | `RunResultStreaming::cancel` |
| 44 | `settings` | Run control | `ModelSettings` temperature + retry, `max_turns` |
| 45 | `model_retry` | Run control | `ModelRetrySettings`: policies, backoff and `retry-after` (offline) |
| 46 | `reasoning` | Run control | Typed `Reasoning` effort/summary for either API |
| 47 | `providers` | Run control | `ProviderRegistry`: route model names to several providers (Rust-only) |

The rest need `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` in the environment; `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and
`OPENAI_API` (`chat_completions` | `responses`) are optional.

```bash
cargo run -p opai-agents-examples --example hello
cargo run -p opai-agents-examples --example tools

OPENAI_API=responses cargo run -p opai-agents-examples --example tools

EXAMPLE_INPUT="Translate 'Hello' to French and Spanish." \
  cargo run -p opai-agents-examples --example agents_as_tools
HITL_AUTO=approve cargo run -p opai-agents-examples --example hitl

cargo run -p opai-agents-examples --example structured_output
```

(The `-p opai-agents-examples` is needed because the workspace has more than one default member,
so a bare `cargo run --example` cannot tell which package you mean.)

### Web demo

A local web console (axum + SSE) in its own package, [`demo/web`](./demo/web): one chat box over a
multi-agent network, a capability checklist, and a chaos drawer that injects faults. The
examples above follow its checklist.

```bash
cargo run -p opai-agents-web-demo
# then open http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

Uses a real model, so `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` are required (startup fails without
them). Extra variables:

- `DEMO_ADDR` — listen address, default `127.0.0.1:3000`. A non-loopback address prints a warning:
  the demo has no authentication.
- `DEMO_DEBUG` — `1`/`0`. Controls fault injection and `/api/debug/*`. On by default for loopback
  addresses, off otherwise; when off, injected faults in requests are ignored.
- `DEMO_HMR` — `1`/`0`. Live reload of `index.html`: the page is read from disk and the browser
  reloads when the file changes, so front-end edits need no rebuild. On by default in debug builds
  (plain `cargo run`) while debug features are on; release builds serve the embedded copy.

The page has a capability checklist (22 items, lit up as you trigger them) and a debug drawer with
fault presets: LLM errors and retry policies, tool delays and failures, summarizer and session
failures, MCP failures, dropped streams, expired or replayed approvals, and server state reset. The
MCP demo server is this same executable re-run with `--mcp-server`. The demo package builds the
facade's `mcp` feature because of it.

## Standard reference

Vendored tree: [`vendor/openai-agents-python`](./vendor/openai-agents-python) pinned by [`vendor/PINNED_VERSION`](./vendor/PINNED_VERSION) (`v0.23.1`).

```bash
bash scripts/sync_vendor.sh --check
```

(Network note: preferred `git submodule` may fail behind restricted GitHub access; the sync script can download the release tarball.)

## Verification

| Layer | Command |
|-------|---------|
| 0. Format, lints, docs, vendor pin | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` · `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` · `bash scripts/sync_vendor.sh --check` |
| 1. ScriptedModel behavior | `cargo test --no-default-features` |
| 1.5 Property tests (generated inputs) | `cargo test --test property_core` |
| 2. OpenAI HTTP contracts (wiremock) | `cargo test` (default features; needs `openai`) |
| 2.5 Whole request bodies (insta snapshots) | `cargo test --test openai_wiremock` |
| SQLite sessions | `cargo test --features sqlite` |
| MCP interoperability (real Python MCP server) | `cargo test --features mcp --test mcp_interop` (needs the venv, skips without it) |
| 3. Python oracle parity | `.venv/bin/python conformance/run_parity.py --check` then `cargo test --test parity_scenarios` |
| 4. Live endpoint smoke (nightly, non-blocking) | `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` |
| 5. Latency benchmarks | `cargo bench` |
| 6. Line coverage ratchet | `.github/workflows/coverage.yml` |

Shared scenarios live in [`conformance/scenarios/`](./conformance/scenarios/). A scenario only
needs `expect` to run; the `.golden.json` produced by the Python oracle is optional and compared
when present. `--check` fails on drift and never overwrites; regenerate deliberately with
`.venv/bin/python conformance/run_parity.py --write-golden` on a machine that has
`openai-agents==0.23.1` installed.

CI runs every layer on Linux and macOS — see `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and
[`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](./docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#layers).

## MCP tools

Enable the `mcp` feature. Any [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server's tools become tools of
your agent, whichever model you use:

```rust
let server = McpClient::stdio(
    StdioParams::new("npx").args(["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp"]),
)
.tool_filter(ToolFilter::block(["write_file"]))
.shared();
let agent = Agent::new("files").mcp_servers(vec![server.clone()]);
// ... run the agent ...
server.cleanup().await?;
```

`McpClient::streamable_http(StreamableHttpParams::new(url).header("Authorization", "Bearer ..."))`
reaches a remote server. See D-041 in [`docs/DEVIATIONS.md`](./docs/DEVIATIONS.md).

## Other providers

Use any OpenAI-compatible server by passing its base URL and key:

```rust
let model = Arc::new(OpenAIChatCompletionsModel::new(
    "deepseek-chat",
    std::env::var("API_KEY").unwrap(),
    Some("https://api.deepseek.com/v1"),
));
```

The Chat Completions adapter is checked against the Python converter and tolerates common
deviations (tool calls without ids, list-valued `content`, error chunks in a stream). Things that
only OpenAI accepts, such as `stream_options`, are sent to other servers only when you ask
(`ModelSettings.include_usage`). See D-040 in [`docs/DEVIATIONS.md`](./docs/DEVIATIONS.md).

## Keeping context short

Long chats and tool-heavy runs outgrow the model's context. Two provider-neutral tools:

- **Per call (history untouched):** `ToolOutputTrimmer` shortens old tool outputs and
  `ContextWindowTrimmer` drops the oldest turns; set one as `RunConfig.model.input_filter`
  (combine with `chain_input_filters`).
- **Stored history:** wrap a session in `CompactingSession` with a `ModelSummarizer` (any model).
  Old turns become a short summary once the history passes a token or item trigger.

```rust
let session = CompactingSession::new(
    InMemorySession::shared("chat"),
    Arc::new(ModelSummarizer::new(summary_model)),
)
.trigger_tokens(6_000)
.keep_recent_turns(3)
.shared();
```

## Compatibility & deviations

- [`docs/COMPAT.md`](./docs/COMPAT.md) — support matrix
- [`docs/DEVIATIONS.md`](./docs/DEVIATIONS.md) — intentional differences from Python (must stay current)
- [`docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md`](./docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md) — where the SDK is heading: milestones, design decisions, and the improvement backlog
- [`STABILITY.md`](./STABILITY.md) — which parts of the API are stable, and the deprecation policy
- [`CHANGELOG.md`](./CHANGELOG.md) — what changed in each release
- [`docs/MIGRATION-FROM-PYTHON.md`](./docs/MIGRATION-FROM-PYTHON.md) — Python → Rust API mapping and what to write yourself
- [`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](./docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) — commit message format and verification
- [`docs/COMPARISON.md`](./docs/COMPARISON.md) — where this SDK differs from the Python one, Rig and ADK-Rust
- [`llms.txt`](./llms.txt) — the docs as one index for coding assistants ([`llms-full.txt`](./llms-full.txt) is the flat file)

HITL is supported as tool-call *resolution*: a call pauses when `needs_resolution` (Python:
`needs_approval`; fixed or dynamic) says so, and the host resolves it on the `RunState` — approve /
reject (with sticky `always_approve` / `always_reject`), or hand back a result produced elsewhere
with `provide_output` (D-048) — including calls inside `Agent.as_tool` nested runs. The Rust
`RunState` JSON schema `openai-agents-rs/4` is a process-local snapshot format and is intentionally **not**
Python 1.18 wire-compatible (D-012) — use one language per durable state store.

## Still out of scope

OpenAI-hosted capabilities (see [Positioning](#positioning)) and the sandbox runtime.

# Source: docs/COMPAT.md

# Compatibility Matrix

## Python module -> Rust crate

The SDK is a Cargo workspace. `opai-agents` (the facade, `crates/facade`) re-exports
`opai_agents_core::*` plus the optional crates, so every path below is reachable from
`opai_agents::…` without naming the crate — except where a row says otherwise.

`RunConfig` rows below use Python's flat field names; the Rust fields are grouped by topic
(`config.model.settings`, `config.tracing.workflow_name`, ...). See the table in
[MIGRATION-FROM-PYTHON.md](./MIGRATION-FROM-PYTHON.md#runconfig-groups).

| Python (`agents.*`) | Rust crate | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent`, `agent_output`, `result`, `run`, `run_config`, `run_state`, `run_context` | `opai-agents-core` | `crates/core/src/{agent,agent_output,result,run_context}` 与 `crates/core/src/run/{mod,config}.rs`、`crates/core/src/run_state/` |
| `tool`, `tool_context`, `tool_guardrails`, `function_schema`, `strict_schema` | `opai-agents-core` | `crates/core/src/{tool,tool_guardrails,strict_schema}` |
| `items`, `handoffs`, `guardrail`, `lifecycle`, `usage`, `stream_events` | `opai-agents-core` | `crates/core/src/…` |
| `model_settings`, `models` (the `Model` / `ModelProvider` contracts) | `opai-agents-core` | `crates/core/src/model` (contract only, no HTTP) |
| `context` (trimmers), `memory` (`CompactingSession`) | `opai-agents-core` | `crates/core/src/{context,memory}`; see D13 for why this is not its own crate |
| `tracing` | `opai-agents-core` | `crates/core/src/tracing`; D3 (allowed to depend only on `usage`) |
| `retry` | `opai-agents-core` | `crates/core/src/retry`; `openai_retry_advice` moved to `crates/openai/src/retry_advice.rs` (D7) |
| `models` (OpenAI provider, Responses / Chat Completions) | `opai-agents-openai` | `crates/openai`; facade feature **`openai`** (on by default) |
| `mcp` | `opai-agents-mcp` | `crates/mcp`; the `McpServer` contract stays in core, facade feature **`mcp`** (**off** by default, D6) |
| `extensions` (`sqlite`) / `SqliteSession` | `opai-agents-sessions` | `crates/sessions/src/sqlite.rs`; facade feature `sqlite` |
| — (Rust-only) `FileSession`, `FileRunStateStore` | `opai-agents-sessions` | `crates/sessions`; facade feature `sessions` (**off** by default, X-016 / X-017) |
| — (Rust-only) provider routing and prefixes | `opai-agents-providers` | `crates/providers`; facade feature `providers` |
| — (Rust-only) ready-made tools (web fetch and similar) | `opai-agents-tools` | `crates/tools`; facade features `tools`, `webfetch` |
| — (Rust-only) ready-made guardrails | `opai-agents-guardrails` | `crates/guardrails`; facade feature `guardrails` |
| — (Rust-only) agent teams | `opai-agents-teams` | `crates/teams`; facade feature `teams` |
| — (Rust-only) batched trace export, sinks, metrics | `opai-agents-observability` | `crates/observability`; facade feature `observability` (**off** by default, X-018) |
| `testing` | `opai-agents-testing` | `crates/testing`; re-exported as `opai_agents::testing` (D2) |
| `decorators` (`@function_tool`) | `opai-agents-macros` | `crates/macros`; `#[function_tool]` |
| `realtime`, `voice`, `prompts`, `computer`, `editor`, `repl` | — | Not ported |


Standard reference: `vendor/openai-agents-python` @ **v0.23.1** (`openai-agents==0.23.1`).
Re-sync the vendored tree with `bash scripts/sync_vendor.sh`.

Scope: provider-neutral. The SDK targets any OpenAI Responses / Chat Completions compatible endpoint, so OpenAI-hosted features are not planned (see [DEVIATIONS.md#scope](./DEVIATIONS.md#scope)); they appear below as **X**.

Legend: **X** = out of scope (OpenAI-hosted) · **S** = supported · **P** = partial · **N** = not supported · **D** = intentional deviation (see [DEVIATIONS.md](./DEVIATIONS.md))

## Streaming wire events

`StreamEvent::RawResponse.data` is one Responses API wire event on every backend
(see [DEVIATIONS.md D-011](./DEVIATIONS.md#streaming-wire-contract)). **F** = forwarded verbatim
from the provider, **S** = synthesized by the adapter, **N** = not emitted.

| Event | Responses | Chat Completions | `ScriptedModel` |
|-------|-----------|------------------|-----------------|
| `response.created` | F | S | S |
| `response.output_item.added` / `.done` | F | S | S |
| `response.content_part.added` / `.done` | F | S | S |
| `response.output_text.delta` | F | S | S |
| `response.output_text.done` | F | N (Python's chat handler does not emit it) | S |
| `response.reasoning_summary_part.added` / `.done` | F | S (from `reasoning_content`) | S |
| `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` / `.done` | F | S (from `reasoning_content`) | S |
| `response.reasoning_text.delta` / `.done` | F | S (from `reasoning`) | S |
| `response.function_call_arguments.delta` | F | S | S |
| `response.function_call_arguments.done` | F | N | S |
| `response.completed` | F | S | S |
| `response.refusal.delta` / `.done` | F | S (from `delta.refusal`) | N |
| `response.output_text.annotation.added` | F | N | N |
| MCP / hosted-tool events | F | N | N (hosted tools not planned, D-006) |
| `sequence_number` | forwarded as-is | synthesized, 0-based | synthesized, 0-based |
| `logprobs` payloads | forwarded as-is | `[]` | `[]` |
| `usage` token details | forwarded as-is | cached / reasoning tokens (D-016) | totals only |

No emitter synthesizes `response.in_progress` / `response.queued`; the Responses adapter forwards
them like any other provider event, and it reads the response id out of them when the terminal
`response.completed` never arrives.

## Model settings

`ModelSettings` covers 22 fields: `temperature`, `top_p`, `frequency_penalty`,
`presence_penalty`, `tool_choice` (typed enum), `parallel_tool_calls`, `truncation`, `max_tokens`,
`reasoning`, `verbosity`, `metadata`, `store`, `top_logprobs`, `include_usage`,
`response_include`, `extra_body`, `extra_headers`, `extra_query`, `preserve_raw_usage`,
`extra_args`, `timeout`, `retry`. `resolve()` overlays non-`None` values and merges dictionaries,
matching Python; `retry` is merged field by field (D-034).

`reasoning` is a typed `Reasoning { effort, summary, extra }` (Python: `openai.types.shared.Reasoning`;
unknown effort/summary strings and untyped fields such as `mode` round-trip). Responses sends it as
the `reasoning` object; Chat Completions sends `effort` as `reasoning_effort` and warns about the
untyped fields, like Python. A `:<effort>` suffix on a model name resolved through a provider
(`"o4-mini:high"`) is Rust-only (X-006).

Not ported: `prompt_cache_retention`, `context_management`, `prompt_cache_options` — three
OpenAI-hosted server features (D-017); reach them with `extra_body` / `extra_args` when a server
does support them.

Request-body precedence, highest first (matching Python):

1. `extra_body` — Python hands it to the OpenAI SDK as a nested argument that is merged over the
   body, so it overrides both mapped settings and `extra_args`.
2. mapped settings — `temperature`, `max_output_tokens`, `metadata`, `include`, …
3. `extra_args` — fills only keys nothing else set; a key that collides with a mapped setting or
   a request field such as `model` is an error (D-024), not a silent drop. Python additionally
   requires these keys to be *typed* SDK parameters; arbitrary fields belong in `extra_body`
   (D-025).

`resolve()` replaces every mapping when the override is not `None`, except `extra_args`, whose
dictionaries are merged (`model_settings.py:273`).

## Verification layers

0. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
   `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`, `scripts/sync_vendor.sh --check`
1. `cargo test --no-default-features` — ScriptedModel behavior
2. `cargo test --all-features` — OpenAI HTTP contracts via wiremock, SQLite sessions
2.5 `cargo test --test property_core` — invariants over generated inputs (proptest);
   `cargo test --test openai_wiremock` — whole request bodies (insta snapshots)
3. `.venv/bin/python conformance/run_parity.py --check` then `cargo test --test parity_scenarios`;
   `cargo test --features mcp --test mcp_interop` and `--test chat_convert_parity` need the venv
4. `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` — the examples against a live endpoint, both APIs
5. `cargo bench` — per-turn latency
6. `.github/workflows/coverage.yml` — line coverage ratchet

# Source: docs/DEVIATIONS.md

# Deviations from openai-agents-python (v0.23.1)

Record every intentional or temporary divergence from the standard Python SDK.
Silent behavioral forks are bugs.

Status values: **Aligned** (resolved, kept for history) · **Accepted** (intentional, often a
Rust language difference) · **Gap** (known missing capability, tracked by COMPAT.md).

## Scope

This SDK is **provider-neutral**: it targets any endpoint that implements the OpenAI Responses or
Chat Completions protocol, including third-party models and gateways. It is not a client for the
official OpenAI service. Rule of thumb: a Python feature is in scope when it needs only a
compatible *protocol* (or runs locally in the SDK); it is out of scope when it needs a capability
that OpenAI hosts. Out-of-scope features are **not planned** and are not tracked as gaps.

| Out of scope (not planned) | Why |
|----------------------------|-----|
| Hosted tools: `WebSearchTool`, `FileSearchTool`, `CodeInterpreterTool`, `ImageGenerationTool`, `HostedMCPTool`, computer / shell / `apply_patch` tool types, tool search, `custom` tools | Run on OpenAI's servers or need Responses-only tool types; reimplement them as function tools or local MCP |
| `Agent.prompt` / `Prompt` | References a prompt stored on the OpenAI platform |
| `OpenAIConversationsSession`, `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` (`responses.compact`) | Use OpenAI's Conversations / compaction endpoints. The provider-neutral replacement is `CompactingSession` and the trimming filters (D-039) |
| Cloud trace export, `TracingConfig.api_key` (the field does not exist) | OpenAI traces backend (D-004); bring your own `TracingProcessor` |
| Realtime / voice | OpenAI-specific APIs |
| `RunConfig.sandbox` and `agents.sandbox` | Not tied to OpenAI, but a container / workspace runtime the size of a separate product. Not planned in this crate; a sandboxed tool can be written as a function tool or an MCP server |

Server-side state (`conversation_id`, `previous_response_id`) stays because it is part of the
Responses protocol, but it works only if the provider implements it; Chat Completions rejects it
(D-K).

## Resolved in Phase-2

| ID | Standard location | Rust behavior | Status |
|----|-------------------|---------------|--------|
| B1 | `RunResult.last_agent` | Previously returned the *starting* agent. Now carries the agent that actually finished. | Aligned |
| B4 | `maybe_reset_tool_choice` | Reset now happens at turn start, driven by a tool-use tracker, so it also applies after a turn that ended early via `stop_on_first_tool` / `StopAtTools`. | Aligned |
| B5 | `_build_tool_result_items` | A `stop_on_first_tool` run now records a `ToolCallOutputItem` for *every* tool in the batch, not only the first. | Aligned |
| B6 | `ResponseFunctionToolCall.call_id` | A `function_call` without `call_id` raises `ModelError::Behavior` instead of falling back to `"call"`. | Aligned |
| D-A | `HandoffCallItem` / `HandoffOutputItem` / `ReasoningItem` | Implemented; handoffs and reasoning now produce their own run items. | Aligned |
| D-B | `tracing.handoff_span` | Emitted for every handoff with `from_agent` / `to_agent`. | Aligned |
| D-C | Mixed approval batches | Verified against v0.23.1: Python also executes the calls that do not need approval before pausing, so the Rust behaviour matches. | Aligned |
| D-D | Non-stream `RawResponse` emit | Dead code removed; only the streaming path emits raw events. | Aligned |
| D-E | `flush_traces` | Now calls `TracingProcessor::force_flush` on all installed processors. | Aligned |
| D-F | `RunConfig.tracing_disabled` | Per-run setting is now authoritative for spans as well as the root trace (previously only the global switch was honoured). | Aligned |
| D-G | `TracingProcessor.on_span_start` / `on_trace_start` | `InMemoryProcessor` now records start events. | Aligned |
| D-H | `RunConfig.trace_id` / `group_id` / `trace_metadata` | Supported and forwarded to `Trace`. | Aligned |
| D-I | Default OpenAI API | The crate-wide default is **Chat Completions** (Python: Responses), whatever the base URL, including `api.openai.com`. Order: the provider's own `.api(..)` (`OpenAIProvider`, `CompatibleProvider`), an explicit `set_default_openai_api(..)`, then Chat Completions. `MultiProvider` has `openai_chat_completions/...` and `openai_responses/...` prefixes to pick per model. Reason: this SDK targets any server that speaks the OpenAI protocol, and nearly all implement Chat Completions while few implement Responses; a wrong guess in the other direction fails on the first request. Consequence: Responses-only features (`previous_response_id`, `conversation_id`, server-side state) need `.api(Responses)` or `set_default_openai_api(Responses)`. The example harness's `OPENAI_API` still overrides | Accepted |
| D-J | `ModelTracing.ENABLED_WITHOUT_DATA` | Driven by `RunConfig.trace_include_sensitive_data` (env `OPENAI_AGENTS_TRACE_INCLUDE_SENSITIVE_DATA`). | Aligned |
| D-K | Chat Completions + `conversation_id` | Returns `ModelError::Unsupported` instead of silently dropping it. | Aligned |
| B7 | `default_tool_error_function` / `failure_error_function` | A tool that returns `Err` no longer aborts the run: the model receives `DEFAULT_TOOL_ERROR_MESSAGE` (the error text is not exposed). `FunctionTool::with_failure_error_function` formats it, `raise_on_error()` restores abort (Python: `failure_error_function=None`). The formatter is synchronous | Aligned |
| B8 | `turn_resolution.py` handoff execution | A turn with a handoff now runs its sibling function tools first, then the first handoff; later handoffs get a `ToolCallOutputItem` with `"Multiple handoffs detected, ignoring this one."`. Every call id has an output. Handoffs take precedence over `tool_use_behavior` stops, as in Python | Aligned |
| B9 | `InputGuardrail.run_in_parallel` | `run_in_parallel(false)` guardrails finish before the first model call and trip without calling the model. Parallel guardrails race the model call: a tripwire drops the in-flight call instead of waiting for it | Aligned |
| B10 | `RunConfig.tool_not_found_behavior` | Unknown tool raises `ModelError::Behavior("Tool X not found in agent Y")`; `ToolNotFoundBehavior::ReturnErrorToModel` answers `"Tool 'X' not found."` and continues | Aligned |
| D-M | `RunConfig.call_model_input_filter` | Ported as an async closure over `CallModelData { model_data, agent, context }` returning `Result<ModelInputData, AgentsError>`; applied before the LLM hooks, for one call only. Python passes the raw context value; Rust passes the `RunContextWrapper`. Python also deduplicates input items afterwards; Rust does not | Aligned |
| D-N | Chat Completions without `usage` | The request still counts (`Usage.requests = 1`, zero tokens), as in Python; a Responses reply without `usage` stays at 0 requests, also as in Python. Previously both reported 0 | Aligned |
| B11 | `Handoff.get_transfer_message` | The handoff output text was `{"assistant":"B"}`; Python's `json.dumps` gives `{"assistant": "B"}`. The model reads this text, so it is now rendered with Python's separators | Aligned |
| D-035 | `RunConfig.reasoning_item_id_policy` | `Option<ReasoningItemIdPolicy>` (`Preserve` / `Omit`). `Omit` strips the `id` of reasoning items in the next turn's input, in `RunResult::to_input_list`, in session saves and in `RunErrorData`; checked against Python. The policy is not stored in `RunState`, so a resumed run uses the policy of the `RunOptions` it is resumed with. Python also drops a `status: null` key from items; Rust keeps items as the provider returned them | Aligned |
| D-036 | `RunConfig.output_guardrail_blocked_message` | `OutputGuardrailBlockedMessage::{Text, Formatter}`; an empty `Text` is a `UserError` when the run starts. When an output guardrail rejects a final output that came from a tool (`stop_on_first_tool`, `StopAtTools`, a custom `ToolUseBehavior`), the `OutputGuardrailTripwireTriggered` result carries the placeholder as `agent_output` and a null `output_info`; a formatter returning `None` / an empty string or panicking falls back to `OUTPUT_GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED_TOOL_OUTPUT`. Model-authored text is never withheld. Checked against Python. The session gets the same data-free record (checked against Python on six scenarios): the withheld turn's tool calls are saved, every tool output of that turn is saved as the placeholder, the model's own messages in that turn are not saved, and a turn that holds a reasoning item is not saved at all; earlier turns keep their real outputs. Not ported: Python also rewrites `new_items`, raw responses and tool guardrail results of the failed run; the Rust error carries only the guardrail result, so there is no other copy to scrub. The formatter is synchronous, as in Python | Aligned |
| D-037 | `task_span` / `turn_span` / `RunConfig.tracing` | `TaskSpanData` / `TurnSpanData` are `SpanData::Task` / `SpanData::Turn`, and `Span.parent_id` is new. The runner builds the same tree as Python (checked on three scenarios: tools plus handoff, `include_task_and_turn_spans: false`, input and output guardrails): task, then one agent span per agent (replaced on handoff), then a turn span per turn; function, handoff, generation and input-guardrail spans sit under the turn, output guardrails under the agent. Task and turn spans export `usage` like Python (`requests` / `total_tokens` on the task only; omitted when all zero). `TracingConfig { include_task_and_turn_spans }`; Python's `api_key` is left out because cloud export is out of scope (D-004). An agent used as a tool (`Agent::as_tool`) starts a run whose task, agent and turn spans nest under the calling tool's function span, as in Python (checked on the same tree; parallel agent tools each keep their own parent, because the current span is scoped to the tool call's future rather than set globally). Differences: spans a user creates outside a run have no parent; the agent span has no `handoffs` / `tools` / `output_type` fields; input guardrails now start inside the first turn, blocking ones before the parallel ones are spawned, as Python does | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-038 | `SQLiteSession` | `SqliteSession` behind the `sqlite` cargo feature (`rusqlite`, bundled SQLite): `in_memory(id)`, `open(id, path)`, `open_with_tables(...)`. Uses Python's schema (`agent_sessions`, `agent_messages(message_data JSON)`, the `(session_id, id)` index, WAL for files), and a database file written by either SDK is read by the other (tested against the Python oracle). `get_items` limit, unreadable-row skipping and `pop_item` follow Python. One shared connection behind a mutex, each call on the blocking pool; table names are restricted to plain identifiers (`UserError` otherwise; Python splices them unchecked). Not ported: `SessionSettings` stored on the session (use `RunConfig.session_settings`), `close()` (the connection closes when the last clone drops), cross-process write-lock tuning, compaction snapshots. Extension point: implement the `Session` trait for any other store | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-039 | Context trimming and compaction (`agents.extensions.ToolOutputTrimmer`; replaces the OpenAI-only `OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession`) | New provider-neutral module `context` plus `CompactingSession`. **Trimming** (per model call, history untouched, usable as `RunConfig.call_model_input_filter`): `ToolOutputTrimmer` is a port checked against Python on three configurations (Unicode, unknown call ids, `trimmable_tools`); not ported are structured-output and `tool_search_output` trimming, which only exist for OpenAI-hosted flows. `ContextWindowTrimmer` (new) drops whole oldest turns to fit `max_tokens` and/or `max_turns`; system / developer messages, a summary and the latest turn always stay. `chain_input_filters` composes them. **Compaction** (rewrites the stored history): `CompactingSession` wraps any `Session`; when the history passes `trigger_tokens` (default 8000 estimated) or `trigger_items`, turns older than `keep_recent_turns` (default 2) are replaced by one summary written by a `Summarizer` (`ModelSummarizer` asks any `Model`), merged with earlier notes. A turn starts at a user message, so a tool call is never separated from its output. The summary is a plain `user` message wrapped in `<conversation_summary>` tags, accepted by every provider. Needs `Session::replace_items` (atomic for `InMemorySession` and `SqliteSession`; the default clears then appends). Differences from Python: it does not call `responses.compact` and has no `compaction_mode`; a failed compaction logs a warning and keeps the history; summarizer calls are not part of the run's `Usage` (read `Summarizer::usage()` / `CompactingSession::summarizer_usage()`, which `ModelSummarizer` fills); each one is a `conversation_summary` custom span under the turn of the run whose save triggered it, except the summary caused by a run's last save, which happens after the trace has ended and emits no span; token counts are an estimate (about 4 ASCII chars or 1 other char per token) unless a counter is supplied; writes are serialized per `CompactingSession`, not across processes | Aligned (new feature) |
| D-040 | Third-party compatibility of the Chat Completions and Responses adapters | The adapters must work with any server that speaks the protocol, so this audit compared them with Python's `chatcmpl_converter` and fixed what broke. Conversion lives in `model::openai::chat_convert` (`items_to_chat_messages`, `chat_message_to_output_items`; public, pure JSON) and is checked against Python on 41 shared cases (`conformance/chat_convert_cases.json`, run through `conformance/chat_convert_oracle.py`). **Fixed**: consecutive function calls and the assistant text around them are one assistant message (they were one message per call, which strict servers reject); typed user messages (`input_text` parts) kept no text; image / file / audio parts, refusals and non-string tool outputs; unknown items are an error instead of silently dropped; `json_schema.name` is `final_output` for both APIs (it was the Rust type path, which OpenAI rejects); `stream_options.include_usage` is only sent by default to `api.openai.com`, so third-party servers that reject it work (set `ModelSettings.include_usage` to force it); a reply `refusal` is kept; `finish_reason` `content_filter` with an empty message becomes a refusal and `length` a `ModelBehaviorError`, in both modes; streamed `delta.refusal`; a `data: {error}` chunk is an error; `reasoning_content` of a tool-calling turn is replayed for DeepSeek models (`OpenAIChatCompletionsModel::should_replay_reasoning_content` overrides the rule). **Beyond Python** (for non-conforming servers): reply `content` may be a list of parts, tool call `arguments` may be a JSON object, and a tool call without an `id` (streamed or not) gets a generated `call_...` id because the runner pairs results by id; an assistant message without an `id` and with `output_text` parts is accepted. **Provider data** (checked against Python on 16 more shared cases, 38 + 19 in all): items a Chat Completions reply produces record `provider_data` (`model`, `response_id`), so reasoning is only sent back to the model that wrote it (the DeepSeek rule now also checks the origin, as Python's does); the `reasoning` field is kept on the item and replayed to the same model; a Gemini `thought_signature` (`tool_calls[].extra_content.google`, plain and streamed, also `provider_specific_fields` for Gemini models) is kept on the function call and restored for Gemini models; Claude `thinking_blocks` are kept on the reasoning item and sent back with `OpenAIChatCompletionsModel::preserve_thinking_blocks(true)` (off by default, like Python's OpenAI adapter, which only its LiteLLM adapter turns on). The Responses adapter removes the placeholder id, `provider_data` and other providers' reasoning from its input, so a run that moves between a Chat Completions and a Responses model (a handoff, say) stays valid. **Not ported**: streamed `thinking_blocks` deltas (LiteLLM-style Claude streaming; plain replies are handled), `item_reference`, `file_search_call`, audio / video parts. Python errors surface as `ModelError::Unsupported`. Pinned by `tests/third_party_compat.rs` (11 wiremock scenarios, all failing on the previous code) | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-041 | `agents.mcp` (`MCPServerStdio`, `MCPServerStreamableHttp`, `MCPUtil`, `Agent.mcp_servers`, `Agent.mcp_config`) | New `mcp` support: the `McpServer` trait, `McpTool` / `McpCallToolResult`, `McpConfig` and the tool conversion live in `opai-agents-core` and are always available; the client, transports, `ToolFilter`, `RequireApproval` and `McpServerManager` are in the `opai-agents-mcp` crate, behind the `mcp` cargo feature of `opai-agents` (**off by default**, so a build that never talks to an MCP server compiles no process or HTTP code for it). `McpClient::stdio(StdioParams)` and `McpClient::streamable_http(StreamableHttpParams)` implement `McpServer`; `Agent::mcp_servers` lists their tools again every turn and turns them into function tools, so they work with any model. Tested against the official Python `mcp` package (`conformance/mcp_server.py`, 10 interoperability tests over stdio and over HTTP with both SSE and plain-JSON replies) and against the Python SDK's own conversion (`conformance/mcp_oracle.py`: names, descriptions and parameter schemas are identical). Ported: tool listing with pagination, `cache_tools_list` / `invalidate_tools_cache`, static and dynamic `ToolFilter`, `RequireApproval::{Never, Always, PerTool}` mapped to `needs_approval`, `use_structured_content`, `convert_schemas_to_strict` (a schema that cannot be made strict is used as is), required-argument check before the call, duplicate tool names across servers are a `UserError`, a result flagged `isError` is shown to the model like any other. **Differences**: a server connects on first use (`connect()` is optional; Python needs `connect()` / `async with`); a dead connection is replaced on the next call; the default request timeout is 30 s (Python: `client_session_timeout_seconds` = 5 s) because it also covers the first request, which for a stdio server includes process start-up and for a remote server a cold connection, and a tool call that legitimately runs longer than 5 s should not fail by default (`McpClient::request_timeout` sets any value); a stdio server inherits only a safe subset of this process's environment, like Python's `get_default_environment`, and the child is killed when the client is dropped; a tool result becomes one string (text blocks joined by newlines, an image as `[image: <mime type>]`, other blocks as JSON) instead of Python's list of tool output parts, because Chat Completions tool messages carry text only; tool failures reach the model through the usual tool-error path (B7), so an exception inside a server tool does not abort the run. **Also ported**: `max_retry_attempts` / `retry_backoff` (`McpClient`; every request is retried with `base * 2^(n-1)` backoff, `-1` retries forever, default none, as Python), and `McpServerManager` (connect a group up front with a timeout, keep the working servers, `failed_servers` / `errors` / `reconnect(failed_only)` / `cleanup_all`, `strict`, `drop_failed_servers`, optional parallel connect; Python's async context manager becomes explicit `connect_all()` / `cleanup_all()` calls, and it does not run each server in its own task). **Not ported**: the legacy SSE transport, prompts and resources, `include_server_in_tool_names`, `tool_meta_resolver` / custom data, tool guardrails on a server, the `mcp_tools_span` trace span, OAuth. `HostedMCPTool` is out of scope (D-006) | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-L | Error source chain | `AgentsError::Tool` / `Internal` carry an optional `#[source]`; helpers `tool_with_source` / `internal_with_source` exist. | Aligned |

## Accepted deviations

| ID | Standard location | Rust behavior | Reason | Plan to align |
|----|-------------------|---------------|--------|---------------|
| D-001 | `Runner.run_sync` | `Runner::run_blocking` works from any thread: with no runtime it uses a shared lazily started multi-thread runtime (no runtime per call, connection pools survive); inside a multi-thread runtime it uses that runtime through `block_in_place`; inside a current-thread runtime it runs on the shared runtime from a helper thread. `Runner::run_blocking_on(&Handle, ...)` picks the runtime (multi-thread handles only, `UserError` otherwise). A panic in the run reaches the caller. Pinned by `tests/behavior_blocking.rs` (plain threads, multi-thread and current-thread runtimes, a custom handle). Differences: from a current-thread runtime the caller's runtime is stalled while it waits, and a run that depends on that stalled runtime (a client bound to it) would not finish; Python's `run_sync` refuses to run inside a running loop instead | Rust has no ambient asyncio loop, and a per-call runtime panics when nested and breaks pooled connections when dropped | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-002 | `@function_tool` docstring → JSON schema | `#[function_tool]` derives the schema from Rust types via `schemars`; the function doc comment becomes the tool description and `///` docs on fields become property descriptions | Rust has no runtime docstrings/annotations | Accepted |
| D-003 | `Agent.handoffs` / `handoff()` | Supported: `input_filter` (per handoff, or `RunConfig.handoff_input_filter`; the handoff's own wins), `on_handoff` (`with_on_handoff`, or `with_on_handoff_input(schema, f)` which replaces `input_type`: the schema is made strict and advertised, the arguments only have to parse as JSON and are not validated against it), and `nest_handoff_history` (`RunConfig.nest_handoff_history`, off by default like Python, per-handoff override `with_nest_handoff_history`, `RunConfig.handoff_history_mapper`, `nest_handoff_history()` / `default_handoff_history_mapper()` / `*_conversation_history_wrappers()` helpers). Verified against Python by the `handoff_nested_history` / `handoff_raw_history` parity scenarios, which compare the exact input the target agent's model receives. Differences: `HandoffInputData` is flattened to Responses input items (`input_history` / `pre_handoff_items` / `new_items`) and has no `input_items` / `NestedHistoryOwnedItem` provenance, so a filter changes only the next agent's input and `RunResult.new_items` stays unfiltered. Python's result is not simply filtered either: with `remove_all_tools` its `new_items` lost the handoff call and output items but kept the earlier tool call items, and `to_input_list()` ended up without the handoff items, so the model input is the contract and the full record stays on `RunResult`; `nest_handoff_history()` returns empty `pre_handoff_items` and `new_items` (the nested `input_history` is the whole input); the history mapper is synchronous (as in Python) and the filter is async; summary JSON follows pydantic field order only for the common Responses item types (`message`, `output_text`, `function_call`, `function_call_output`, `reasoning`, summary / reasoning text), other item types keep the provider's key order; a filter with `conversation_id` / `previous_response_id` raises `UserError`, and nesting there is disabled with a warning, as in Python | Aligned (provenance not ported) |
| D-004 | OpenAI `BackendSpanExporter` / `set_tracing_export_api_key` (cloud trace export) | Not implemented and not planned: spans go to local / in-memory processors, and users who want a backend implement `TracingProcessor` (OTLP, Langfuse, ...). Decision recorded 2026-10 | The Traces dashboard is the only loss; no model behavior depends on it | Accepted (won't do) |
| D-005 | `Runner.run_streamed` | `Runner::run_streamed` + `RunResultStreaming` | Naming only; the raw event vocabulary matches Python (D-011) | Aligned |
| D-006 | MCP / hosted tools / sandbox | Not exported. **Hosted tools** (`WebSearchTool`, `FileSearchTool`, `CodeInterpreterTool`, `ImageGenerationTool`, `HostedMCPTool`) are executed by OpenAI's servers on the Responses API; supporting them needs a tool enum, new serialized tool types and new output items, and is **not planned** (decision 2026-10). Local MCP servers are supported (D-041); the sandbox is not planned (Scope table). Sessions are covered by D-027 | Function tools cover local execution; hosted capabilities must be reimplemented as function tools | Accepted (hosted tools out of scope, see Scope) |
| D-007 | Package layout | Cargo workspace of twelve crates: `opai-agents-core` (agents, tools, handoffs, HITL, guardrails, the run loop), `opai-agents-openai` (Responses and Chat Completions adapters), `opai-agents-mcp`, `opai-agents-providers`, `opai-agents-sessions` (which also holds the SQLite backend behind its `sqlite` feature), `opai-agents-observability`, `opai-agents-tools`, `opai-agents-guardrails`, `opai-agents-teams`, `opai-agents-testing`, `opai-agents-macros`, and the `opai-agents` facade that re-exports them behind Cargo features. `core` has no network, database or subprocess dependency (`scripts/check_module_deps.py` enforces it). The runner is a module directory under `crates/core/src/run/` (`agent_loop` validates options and opens the trace, `turn_loop` holds the per-turn phases, `finalize`, `turn/`, `tools/`) | The split keeps the no-HTTP build (`cargo test --no-default-features`) a real check. Python keeps one package and splits the same code across `run.py` and `run_internal/` | N/A (aligned intent) |
| D-008 | Default max turns `10` | Same default (`DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 10`) | — | Aligned |
| D-009 | `function_tool` `failure_error_function`, `RunConfig.tool_error_formatter` | Per-tool `failure_error_function` is ported (B7), synchronous only. `RunConfig.tool_error_formatter` is ported for `approval_rejected` and `tool_not_found` (async closure returning `Option<String>`; `None` keeps the default). `ToolErrorFormatterArgs` has no `tool_type` (all Rust tools are function tools). The default rejection message is stored when `RunState::reject` is called, so an explicit message equal to the default text is formatted too | Accepted |
| D-010 | Prefer git submodule for vendor | Vendored via release tarball + `vendor/PINNED_VERSION`, refreshed by `scripts/sync_vendor.sh` | The vendored tree is the parity oracle (`conformance/setup_venv.sh`); a tarball pins the exact release without a submodule checkout step and works without access to the upstream git remote | Prefer submodule when accessible |
| D-011 | Token-level `RawResponsesStreamEvent` from `Model.stream_response` | `StreamEvent::RawResponse.data` is a standard Responses wire event, matching Python's `RawResponsesStreamEvent.data`. Responses forwards provider events verbatim (`openai_responses.py:781`); Chat Completions synthesizes them the way `chatcmpl_stream_handler.py` does; `ScriptedModel` replays a step the way `testing/model.py` does. See [Streaming wire contract](#streaming-wire-contract) | Not ported: `response.output_text.annotation.added` and logprob payloads (emitted empty); `response.refusal.delta` / `.done` are synthesized (D-040); usage token details are emitted (D-016) | Aligned |
| D-012 | Python `RunState` schema 1.18 wire format | Rust schema `openai-agents-rs/4` via `to_json`/`from_json` (`/3`, `/2` and the pre-rename ids still load); sticky `always_approve`/`always_reject`; `Agent.as_tool` nested HITL | Not byte-compatible with Python snapshots. A paused run is resumed by the Rust SDK that paused it; only a deployment where a Rust and a Python process hand a paused run to each other would need the Python format, and none is known. The pre-rename ids `openai-agents-rust/1` and `openai-agents-rust/2` are still accepted on load. `/3` made `max_turns` an `Option<usize>` so an unlimited run can pause and resume (D-042); a `/2` payload carries a number, which loads as `Some(n)`, and only `/3` and later may carry `null`. `/4` is the current id: call resolutions moved from `approvals` to `resolutions` and an entry may carry an `output`, and paused-call items are tagged `tool_interruption` (was `tool_approval`); `/3` payloads load unchanged (D-048) | Accepted (revisit only if cross-SDK resume is needed) |
| D-013 | `MultiProvider` provider registry | Only `openai` and `openai_chat_completions` prefixes are built in; others are registered explicitly. `CompatibleProvider::new(base_url)` is the provider-neutral way to add one: optional key (no `Authorization` header without it), Chat Completions by default, `.api(..)`, `.default_model(..)`. `OpenAIProvider::from_env` accepts a missing key when `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is set. Pinned by `tests/compatible_provider.rs` | No dynamic entry-point discovery in Rust; a registry of named endpoints covers the same need explicitly | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-022 | `ScriptedModel.set_default_usage` | Applies to steps whose usage is empty, matching Python | — | Aligned |
| D-014 | `RunContextWrapper[TContext]` | Context is type-erased (`Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>`) with `context::<T>()` / `try_context::<T>()` | Avoids threading a generic parameter through `Agent` / `Runner`; type errors surface at runtime, mitigated by an explicit error message | Accepted |
| D-015 | `Agent.hooks` / `RunHooks` default implementations | Provided as `async_trait` methods with empty bodies, so implementors override only what they need | Same shape as Python base classes | Accepted |
| D-016 | `Usage` token details | `Usage` carries `input_tokens_details` (`cached_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`), `output_tokens_details` (`reasoning_tokens`) and `request_usage_entries`, aggregated by `add` like Python. Both OpenAI adapters fill them (Responses `*_tokens_details`; Chat `prompt_tokens_details` / `completion_tokens_details`), `total_tokens` is the provider's value, and `response.completed` carries the details. Not ported: `preserve_raw_usage` (D-017), per-request details from adapter-private attributes. Loading an older `RunState` without details defaults them to 0 | Aligned |
| D-017 | `ModelSettings` non-portable fields | `extra_query` and `preserve_raw_usage` are ported: `extra_query` is appended to the request URL of both APIs (scalars as text, arrays repeat the key, `null` skipped), `preserve_raw_usage` keeps the provider's `usage` object on `ModelResponse.raw_usage` (also in `RunState` JSON) for plain and streamed Chat Completions and for Responses, and is empty when the provider sends no usage object. Pinned by `tests/third_party_compat.rs`. Not exposed, and not planned: `prompt_cache_retention`, `context_management` and `prompt_cache_options` configure OpenAI-hosted server features that other servers ignore or reject; `extra_body` / `extra_args` reach any such parameter when a server does support it | Gateways use query strings for API versions and return non-standard usage fields (cost, cache hits), so those two are useful everywhere; the other three are OpenAI-specific | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-024 | `extra_args` collision error type | A colliding `extra_args` key returns `ModelError::Behavior` (surfacing as `AgentsError::Model`) | Python raises a bare `TypeError` from the client call; Rust has no kwargs layer to raise from, so the message mirrors Python's (`… got multiple values for keyword argument 'x'`) and the failure travels through the typed error channel | Accepted |
| D-025 | `extra_args` accepts arbitrary keys | Any key is written straight into the request body | The openai SDK's `create()` has no `**kwargs`: `extra_args` keys must be *typed* SDK parameters (`service_tier`, `prompt_cache_key`, `logprobs`, …) and an unknown key raises `TypeError: … got an unexpected keyword argument`. Arbitrary body fields belong in `extra_body` ("Add additional JSON properties to the request"). Rust has no typed SDK surface to validate against, and an OpenAI-specific allowlist would reject legitimate OpenAI-compatible gateway parameters, so it stays permissive | Accepted — prefer `extra_body` for arbitrary fields |
| D-019 | `agents.testing` has no HTTP mocks | `ScriptedModel` is the only shipped test double. HTTP contract tests live in `tests/openai_wiremock.rs` and drive `wiremock` directly, so no mock layer is part of the public API | Aligns the `testing` surface with Python; the old `MockResponses` / `MockCompletions` wrappers were removed | Accepted |
| D-020 | `ModelStep.responder` / `stream_events` | Not ported; steps are a plain output/error pair. `retry_advice` is ported (`ModelStep::with_retry_advice`, and `raise_model_error` for typed errors) | Test-double features only: they let a test script a step from the request or script raw stream events, and nothing in the runner depends on them | Later phase (low priority) |
| D-021 | `ModelCall` recorded fields | Records `streamed` and `output_schema_name`, but not `output_schema`, `handoffs` or `prompt` objects | Test-assertion detail only; `ModelRequest` does not carry handoffs, and Python exposes the live objects | Later phase (low priority) |
| D-018 | `function_tool` variadic / `Annotated` parameters | Not supported; the macro accepts plain owned-typed identifiers and an optional leading context parameter | Rust signatures cannot express `*args` / `**kwargs` with types | Accepted |
| D-023 | Chat Completions synthesized response id | The synthesized `response` object and `ModelResponse.response_id` carry the provider's `id` (e.g. `chatcmpl-…`) when the gateway sends one; `FAKE_RESPONSES_ID` only when it does not | Python always uses `FAKE_RESPONSES_ID` for Chat Completions. The id is only fed back as `previous_response_id`, which the Chat Completions adapter ignores | Accepted |

## Component deviations (audit 2026-10)

The Plan column is the status here (`None` = nothing left to do). Entries were collected by an
audit, so they mix finished work with remaining gaps; the Rust behavior column says which.

| ID | Standard location | Rust behavior | Plan |
|----|-------------------|---------------|------|
| D-026 | `RunConfig` | Ported: `tracing` (D-037), `output_guardrail_blocked_message` (D-036), `reasoning_item_id_policy` (D-035), `session_input_callback` / `session_settings` (D-027), `tool_execution.max_function_tool_concurrency` (D-029), `nest_handoff_history` / `handoff_history_mapper` (D-003), `tool_name_collision_policy` (D-032), `tool_error_formatter` (D-009), `handoff_input_filter` (D-003), `tool_not_found_behavior` (B10), `model`, `model_provider`, `model_settings`, `input_guardrails`, `output_guardrails`, `tracing_disabled`, `workflow_name`, `trace_id`, `group_id`, `trace_metadata`, `trace_include_sensitive_data`. Missing: `sandbox` (not planned, Scope table) | None |
| D-027 | `Runner.run(session=…)` / `agents.memory` | `Session` trait + `InMemorySession`, passed as `RunOptions.session`, with `RunConfig.session_settings` (`limit`; a session can supply defaults via `Session::session_settings`) and `RunConfig.session_input_callback` (async closure over `(history, new_items)`). History precedes the new input; on completion the run's input and model-visible new items are appended (also for `run_streamed`). Checked against Python's `SQLiteSession` for the limit and callback cases. Saving follows Python (checked on the same scenarios): the input is saved before the first model call and each turn's items when the turn ends, so a run that fails or hits `max_turns` keeps the turns it completed. A run paused for approval has saved the turns before the paused one (`RunState.session_saved_items` / `session_input_saved`, in the JSON too); resuming with the same session saves the rest exactly once, so the final history equals Python's. Python also stores the pending tool call while paused; this SDK keeps the paused turn out of the session until it ends, which avoids a stored call without an output. The model input read from a session is cleaned as in Python: stored function calls without an output are dropped together with the reasoning items that led to them, history outputs whose call a `limit` cut off are dropped, and duplicate items are merged (latest content; calls and reasoning keep their first slot). With a `session_input_callback`, items are attributed to history or to the new input by origin, even when the callback edited them: each item handed to the callback carries a hidden `_agents_session_origin` key that is removed from everything it returns (Python tracks object identity; an item the callback rebuilds loses the key and is matched by content, as in Python). Differences: a callback can see that key in the items it receives; the cleaning covers function calls only (Python also handles OpenAI-hosted call types); provider-neutral compaction is `CompactingSession` (D-039); the OpenAI-hosted sessions are out of scope; `SqliteSession` is available behind the `sqlite` feature (D-038); `RunResult.input` stays the caller's input without history | Other backends: implement `Session` |
| D-028 | `Agent` fields | Missing: async `tool_use_behavior` functions (`ToolsToFinalOutputFunction`; the sync `ToolUseBehavior::Custom` is ported and sees tool name / call id / output only, not the run item), `Agent.clone(**overrides)` (use struct `Clone` + builder), `get_all_tools` | Async custom behavior can follow; `prompt` is out of scope (Scope table) |
| D-029 | `FunctionTool` / `tool_guardrails.py` | Only `FunctionTool` exists (no hosted, computer, shell, apply-patch or custom tools; MCP tools are converted to function tools, D-041). `is_enabled` is `ToolEnabled` (fixed bool or an async closure over `(RunContextWrapper, Arc<Agent>)`; re-evaluated every turn). `timeout_seconds` / `timeout_behavior` / `timeout_error_function` are ported (`with_timeout`, `with_timeout_behavior`, `with_timeout_error_function`; the formatter is synchronous and returns text; the default message formats the number with Rust's `{}`, so very small or large values print as `0.00001` where Python's `:g` prints `1e-05`), as is `RunConfig.tool_execution.max_function_tool_concurrency` (validated when the run starts and reported as `UserError`, where Python raises `ValueError` at construction). Tool input / output guardrails are ported (`FunctionTool::with_tool_input_guardrails` / `with_tool_output_guardrails`, `ToolGuardrailBehavior::{Allow, RejectContent, RaiseException}`, results on `RunResult.tool_input_guardrail_results` / `tool_output_guardrail_results`; behavior checked against Python: a rejection replaces the call, so the start hook, the body and the output guardrails are skipped; output guardrails also see timeout / failure messages; they are skipped while a nested agent tool waits for approval). Differences: results hold the guardrail's name instead of the guardrail object; guardrail data holds the `ToolContext` and `Arc<Agent>`. Input, tool input and tool output guardrail results gathered before a pause are kept in `RunState` (also in its JSON) and appear on the resumed run's result, and a resumed run no longer runs the input guardrails again (it did before; Python runs them once, checked: one call, one result after resume). Not ported: `pre_approval_tool_input_guardrails`, `defer_loading` / namespaces | Rest as listed |
| D-030 | `Handoff` | `Agent.handoffs` takes `Handoff` only (Python also accepts a bare `Agent`). `is_enabled` is supported like tools; no `on_invoke_handoff` override (D-003 covers `input_filter` / `on_handoff`). The target of `handoff(agent)` is owned (`Arc<Agent>` by value), so it cannot point back up the graph; cycles (A to B to A) are built with `handoff_to_name("A")`, a late-bound handoff the runner resolves by name among the agents reachable from the starting agent and every agent it has switched to (`UserError` when none matches; the stand-in has no `handoff_description`, so use `with_tool_description`). Checked against a Python cycle (same final output, last agent and call counts). Python expresses the loop by mutating `handoffs` after construction, which Rust's owned graph cannot do | Python shares agents by reference; an owned graph is what keeps `Agent` a plain cloneable value | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-031 | `RunResultStreaming.cancel(mode)` | `cancel(CancelMode::Immediate / AfterTurn)` and `is_cancelled()`. Immediate aborts the run task, which also aborts the child tasks it spawned (parallel input guardrails, the raw-event forwarder; they are held in an abort-on-drop wrapper) and closes the queue; AfterTurn stops before the next turn. A cancelled run has no `final_output`. Dropping the stream does **not** cancel the run, as in Python (the task keeps running); `RunResultStreaming::cancel_on_drop(true)` opts in to cancelling when the handle is dropped, for consumers such as a disconnected SSE client. The event queue holds 64 events and is bounded: a consumer slower than the model makes the run wait (Python's queue is unbounded). Pinned by `immediate_cancel_aborts_parallel_input_guardrails` and `cancel_on_drop_is_opt_in` | Python's `cancel()` cancels the whole asyncio task tree; tokio tasks are detached from their parent, so the wrapper reproduces that. `cancel_on_drop` is an addition: the default stays Python's | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-032 | `RunConfig.tool_name_collision_policy` | `ToolNameCollisionPolicy::Warn` (default) / `Error`, evaluated every turn before the model call. Warn logs through the `tracing` crate and keeps one winner per name: the last handoff if any, else the last tool. Messages are shorter than Python's (no per-agent derived-name hint). Python's namespace and deferred-tool checks are not applicable | Aligned |
| D-033 | `run_error_handlers` | `RunOptions.error_handlers` has `max_turns`, `model_refusal` and `invalid_final_output` (`on_*` builders; async closures returning `Result<Option<RunErrorHandlerResult>>`; `None` raises the original error). `RunErrorHandlerInput.error` is `RunHandledError::{MaxTurns, ModelRefusal, InvalidFinalOutput}`. The output is validated against a structured `output_type` (`UserError` if invalid), recorded as an assistant message unless `include_in_history` is false, then the end hooks and output guardrails run. New `AgentsError::ModelRefusal(ModelRefusalError)`: a refusal in the turn's last message ends the run with it, **also for plain-text agents** (Python does the same), unless a handler supplies the output. As in Python, `model_refusal` / `invalid_final_output` handlers see only the current response in `run_data.raw_responses`. An empty structured answer with no handler asks the model again (Python `NextStepRunAgain`; this replaces the earlier Rust behavior error), an unparsable one raises `ModelBehaviorError`. Checked against Python by the `max_turns_handler` and `refusal_raises` parity scenarios and by direct runs. Differences: the handler must return `RunErrorHandlerResult` (no bare-value / dict forms); Python's data-redaction mode for these errors is not ported; refusals are recognized in the `refusal` content part of Responses messages and, for Chat Completions, in `message.refusal` and `finish_reason: content_filter` (D-040) | Aligned (except as listed) |
| D-042 | `RunOptions.max_turns = None` | Python documents `max_turns` as "Set to `None` to disable the limit" (`run_config.py:591-592`) and only compares when it is not `None` (`run.py:1507`). Rust resolved `options.max_turns.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS)`, so `None` silently became 10. **Fixed**: `max_turns` stays `Option<usize>` through the loop, the comparison is skipped when it is `None`, and `RunState.max_turns` became `Option<usize>` so a paused unlimited run resumes unlimited (schema `openai-agents-rs/3`; a `/2` number loads as `Some(n)`). `RunOptions::default()` still sets `Some(10)` (D-008). Pinned by `max_turns_none_disables_the_limit` and `unlimited_run_state_round_trip_keeps_max_turns_null` | Aligned |
| D-043 | `Agent.as_tool(...)` keyword surface | `AsToolConfig` carries `name` / `description` / `needs_resolution` (Python: `needs_approval`, D-048) / `max_turns` / `on_stream` (`run/as_tool.rs`, struct `AsToolConfig`). `on_stream` runs the nested agent in streaming mode and awaits the handler for each event, in order, so a slow handler slows the nested run (backpressure through the run's 64-event channel) instead of filling a queue; Python's `on_stream_max_pending_events` and `_AgentToolStreamOverflow` therefore do not exist here. The event carries the agent's name, not the agent, and the tool call's name and id, not the call object. Dropping the tool call cancels only the nested run. Not ported: `custom_output_extractor`, `is_enabled`, `run_config`, `hooks`, `previous_response_id`, `conversation_id`, `session`, `failure_error_function`, and the structured-input trio `parameters` / `input_builder` / `include_input_schema`. The nested run therefore always uses `RunOptions::default()` (its own 10-turn budget, no context, no session) and the tool's output is the nested `final_output` verbatim | Later phase. `run_config` / `hooks` / `session` / `failure_error_function` are mechanical; `parameters` needs a typed-input builder |
| D-044 | Function tool output parts (`ToolOutputText` / `ToolOutputImage` / `ToolOutputFileContent`) | Python converts a structured tool return into `input_text` / `input_image` / `input_file` content parts (`items.py:946-1031`). Rust has one JSON value per tool result and renders it with `value_to_tool_string` (`run.rs:2977`), so a tool cannot hand an image or a file to the model. MCP results are flattened to one string for the same reason (D-041) | Later phase: needs a richer `ToolResult.output` and a per-API content-part writer. Chat Completions tool messages carry text only, so the value is limited to the Responses path |
| D-045 | `RunOptions.auto_previous_response_id` | Not ported. Python's `OpenAIServerConversationTracker` derives `previous_response_id` from the last response the server accepted and repairs a broken chain when resuming (`oai_conversation.py:225-246`). Rust stores whatever `response.response_id` the last call returned (`run.rs:1622-1624`) and has no tracker, so `previous_response_id` must be threaded by hand and a reply without an id breaks the chain | Later phase, tied to the missing server-conversation tracker (which D-034 also names as the reason `rewind` is not ported) |
| D-046 | `RunResult` / exception surface | Not ported: `RunResult.context_wrapper` (the run's `RunContextWrapper` is not exposed on the result), Python's `AgentToolInvocation` metadata on a nested `as_tool` result (`result.py`), and `AgentsException.run_data = RunErrorDetails(...)` (`run.py:2186-2196`), which Python attaches to any exception that escapes a run. Rust passes `RunErrorData` to an `error_handlers` closure but never attaches it to the error itself | Later phase (low priority): `run_data` matters only for callers that catch the error without installing a handler |
| D-047 | Crate layout and the default model provider | The SDK is a Cargo workspace: `opai-agents-core` (agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, run loop, sessions, tracing, the `Model` / `ModelProvider` / `McpServer` contracts), `opai-agents-openai`, `opai-agents-mcp`, `opai-agents-sqlite`, `opai-agents-testing`, `opai-agents-macros`, and `opai-agents`, the facade users depend on, which re-exports them under the paths the SDK has always had.
